The excellent mechanical properties were attributed to the synergistic effects of lattice distortions, reduced dislocation density, weakened texture and refined grain structure.
The flow stresses exhibited typical dynamic recrystallization (DRX) characteristics at elevated temperatures.
The distinctive flow curve shapes, characterized by a peak stress followed by a flow softening regime, suggest the occurrence of dynamic recrystallization (DRX).

A significant increase in dislocation density at the grain boundary was observed due to severe dislocation pile-up surrounding the precipitated phase (Fig. 12 b), which promoted the nucleation of DDRX.

This phenomenon indicates that subgrain rotation nucleation mechanisms occurred during hot deformation, and the subgrain boundaries would further transform the new continuous dynamic recrystallization (CDRX) grains by absorbing dislocations in the interior of original grains.

The high-temperature annealing process facilitates the dissolution of the Al2O3 phase, thereby promoting the re-solid solution of element with a large atomic radius, such as Al, and interstitial impurity like O into the matrix. This leads to an enhanced solid solution strengthening effect.
Grain refinement is a promising approach for simultaneously enhancing the strength and plasticity of materials.
